author: DharmaTrader
text:
Since I'm active during the NY session I've been looking at the possibility of trading futures in addition to forex since things seem to go quiet in forex after the London close. I was looking back at the movements in crude and came across this setup. I decided to post it as a reminder that there are great trades to be had even when we miss the initial move out of HTF S/D.

With this setup we have a spike down into a fresh 4H demand zone. We then get a QM formation on the 1H and have a lengthy CP on the 15M which brings us to the 50% fib and an ignored demand zone.

Given the compression it would have been reasonable to set a limit at the top of the 1H ignored demand which also corresponds with a decision area on the 15M. Stop would be below the 1H demand which is also the QM area (about 35 pips). Expected return would be the top of the CP area which is 100 pips.

Often when I look at a chart and see that a big move has occurred I will say, Oh well, I missed that one and move on. I tend to focus too much on the LTF and this is a good reminder to keep the HTF in focus and look for the opportunity that comes as a result of that big move that I missed.

author: outapips
text:
From time to time I am getting confused as to whats happening with price. I'm continuing to go thru charts and find qm's, rbr's etc but when it comes to reading or following price live I'm having difficulty.

An example below is with uchf. I could follow along well until we rose off the RS and then came back down to support again at the last "X". I would have expected price to go down thru the 0.9745 zone as its been hit many times before and thought any demand left would have been taken out with spike down in the blue circled area at "X".

Price did make a nice tail thru there but I thought this is just clearing the demand out of the way for a move south and that the RS was going to fail. I thought maybe price will go down to the next lower demand level and possibly make a false break and then up.

It's situations like this where I get really confused as its making LH's all the way down.

I would appreciate some comments on what I should have seen while this was unfolding to give me a clue that price would rally off this level again?

Thank you

author: Josh
text:
My 2c - the move from the lows is not a false break - if you zoom in you should see where price reacted and why - it was not a typical false break IMO.

The more obvious false break was at the start of the down move - price reacted at the DBD in the process tripping stops enticing breakout trades above that previous significant swing high.

Remember that just because price has tested a demand or supply zone once doesn't mean that supply/demand it fully consumed.

Also remember to zoom in, higher timeframe charts hide information that can be shown on the lower time frames.
